edges.description: The ichthyosis mouse reproduces the Pelger-Huet-like neutrophil nuclear phenotype.
edges.limitations: The mouse is a complete null modelling the structural (neutrophil) branch; it does not reproduce the human regressive skeletal dysplasia and instead shows alopecia, syndactyly and hydrocephalus.

nodes.description: Reduced sterol C14-reductase activity blocks the Delta14 step of cholesterol biosynthesis, leaving the intermediate cholesta-8,14-dien-3-beta-ol to accumulate and reducing cell-autonomous cholesterol synthesis.

nodes.description: Bowed tubular bones, including femoral bowing, detectable prenatally and regressing over childhood.

evidence.reference_title: Antenatal diagnostic dilemma in a pseudodominant pedigree with lamin-B receptor (LBR)-related regressive spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: sonographic evidence of short and bowed tubular bones with narrow thorax

nodes.description: Impaired cholesterol supply in growth-plate chondrocytes is inferred to disturb endochondral ossification, producing the short, bowed long bones and spondylometaphyseal changes. Residual enzyme activity and paralogue redundancy are thought to permit the later spontaneous radiographic regression.

evidence.reference_title: Lamin B receptor-related disorder is associated with a spectrum of skeletal dysplasia phenotypes.

An anadysplasia-like, spontaneously remitting spondylometaphyseal dysplasia secondary to lamin B receptor (LBR) gene mutations: further definition of the phenotypic heterogeneity of LBR-bone dysplasias.
evidence.snippet: homozygosity or compound heterozygosity of mutations in LBR can result in a mild, spontaneously regressing bone dysplasia

evidence.reference_title: HEM dysplasia and ichthyosis are likely laminopathies and not due to 3beta-hydroxysterol Delta14-reductase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: HEM dysplasia and ichthyosis are laminopathies rather than inborn errors of cholesterol synthesis

nodes.description: Independently of the sterol branch, a reduced dose of the structural LBR protein at the nuclear envelope causes failure of neutrophil nuclear lobulation, seen as the hyposegmented Pelger-Huet neutrophil nuclei. The two branches can be uncoupled - some alleles give skeletal disease without Pelger-Huet anomaly.

evidence.reference_title: Understanding and recognizing the Pelger-Huët anomaly.
evidence.snippet: PHA is caused by a decreased amount of the lamin B receptor (LBR).

evidence.reference_title: Dosage effect of zero to three functional LBR-genes in vivo and in vitro.
evidence.snippet: Our data demonstrate that there is a highly significant gene-dosage effect between the gene copy number and the nuclear segmentation index of neutrophils.

nodes.description: Hyposegmented, bilobed "pince-nez" neutrophil nuclei (Pelger-Huet anomaly), usual but not invariant; harmless to neutrophil function in humans.

nodes.description: Biallelic hypomorphic LBR variants reduce 3-beta-hydroxysterol Delta14-reductase (sterol C14-reductase) activity. Missense substitutions in the sterol-reductase domain lower substrate affinity, while truncating alleles destabilise the protein.

evidence.reference_title: The Lamin B receptor is essential for cholesterol synthesis and perturbed by disease-causing mutations.
evidence.snippet: point mutations in the sterol reductase domain perturb enzymatic activity by reducing the affinity

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous variant in the Lamin B receptor gene LBR results in a non-lethal skeletal dysplasia without Pelger-Huët anomaly.
evidence.snippet: demonstrate the effect of this variant on sterol C14-reductase activity

nodes.description: Spontaneous Lbr-null (ichthyosis) mice reproduce the Pelger-Huet-like hyposegmented neutrophils, confirming LBR as the molecular basis of the human anomaly, but their other features (alopecia, syndactyly, hydrocephalus) differ from the human regressive skeletal dysplasia, so the mouse models the neutrophil branch rather than the skeletal one.
Proximal (rhizomelic) shortening of the limbs, prominent prenatally and in infancy, improving over time.

nodes.description: Homozygous c.1534C>T (p.Arg512Trp); reported in a pseudodominant pedigree with fetal-onset disease and associated with Pelger-Huet anomaly.

nodes.description: Homozygous c.1366C>G (p.Leu456Val); causes the skeletal dysplasia without Pelger-Huet anomaly, uncoupling the two branches.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous variant in the Lamin B receptor gene LBR results in a non-lethal skeletal dysplasia without Pelger-Huët anomaly.
evidence.snippet: We identified a homozygous LBR missense mutation (NM_002296.4: c.1366C > G, p.(Leu456Val)) in two adult sisters with a Lamin B receptor-related disorder associated with a skeletal dysplasia milder than Greenberg Dysplasia.
